content: Betrixaban therapy was evaluated in patients with severe renal insufficiency (defined as a creatinine clearance of 15-29 mL/min) who required the concurrent use of a P-glycoprotein (P-gp) inhibitor. The efficacy of betrixaban was determined based on a composite outcome, which included the occurrence of any of the following events up to the Day 35 visit: asymptomatic proximal deep vein thrombosis (DVT) detected via ultrasound, symptomatic proximal or distal DVT, non-fatal pulmonary embolism (PE), or death related to venous thromboembolism (VTE). Efficacy analyses were conducted using the modified Intent-to-Treat (mITT) population. This population included all patients who had taken at least one dose of the study drug and had follow-up assessment data for at least one primary or secondary efficacy outcome component. A total of 7,441 patients were included in the mITT population, with 3,721 patients in the betrixaban group and 3,720 in the enoxaparin group. The efficacy results for the APEX trial are detailed in the study findings. For patients randomized to the 80 mg betrixaban dose group within the mITT population, the primary efficacy analysis results are provided in the study. Patients who were randomized to receive 40 mg of betrixaban (those with severe renal impairment or those receiving P-gp inhibitors) demonstrated VTE rates comparable to those in the enoxaparin group (6 to 14 days of enoxaparin followed by placebo). Betrixaban capsules are supplied in two dosages: The 40 mg capsules are light grey with 40 printed in black and have a light blue cap with PTLA printed in white. They are available in bottles of 100 (NDC 69853-0202-1). The 80 mg capsules are light grey with 80 printed in black and have a blue cap with PTLA printed in white. They are available in bottles of 100 (NDC 69853-0201-1). Storage instructions specify that betrixaban should be stored at room temperature, between 20°C and 25°C (68°F to 77°F). Patient Counseling Information: 1. Risk of Bleeding: Inform patients that betrixaban may prolong bleeding time, and they may bruise or bleed more easily. Advise patients to report any unusual bleeding to their physician. Instruct patients to inform their physicians and dentists that they are taking betrixaban or any other products that affect bleeding (including over-the-counter products like aspirin or NSAIDs) before undergoing any surgery, medical, or dental procedures, or before starting any new medication. 2. Use in Patients with Severe Renal Impairment: Inform patients that the risk of bleeding is higher in individuals with severe kidney problems (severe renal impairment). 3. Spinal/Epidural Hematoma: Advise patients undergoing neuraxial anesthesia or spinal puncture to monitor for signs and symptoms of spinal or epidural hematomas, such as leg numbness or weakness, or bowel or bladder dysfunction. Instruct patients to contact their physician immediately if these symptoms occur. 4. Pregnancy and Lactation: Advise female patients to inform their physicians if they are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, breastfeeding, or intending to breastfeed while on betrixaban therapy. 5. How to Take Betrixaban: Instruct patients to take betrixaban with food. Provide guidance on what to do if a dose is missed. Precautions with Alcohol: The interaction between alcohol and betrixaban has not been established. Patients should consult their physician regarding the effects of consuming alcohol while taking this medication. Brand Name: Betrixaban is marketed under the brand name BEVYXXA. Look-Alike Drug Names: There is limited information available regarding potential look-alike drug names for betrixaban in the drug label.
